1. Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.

2.  The present petition has been filed under Section 482 Cr.PC seeking quashing of the FIR No.1100/2020 under Sections 498A/46/34 IPC registered at PS Nihal Vihar, Delhi and the proceedings pursuant thereto, on the ground that the parties have arrived at a settlement.
3. Issue notice.
Learned APP for the State accepts notice.
He submits that since the present FIR has arisen out of a matrimonial dispute and the parties have amicably settled all their disputes, the State has no objection in case the present FIR is quashed.
4. The petitioner no.1 (former husband), petitioner no.2 (father of the petitioner no.1), petitioner no.3 (mother of the petitioner no.1) and the This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 24/09/2023 at 17:21:56 petitioner no.4 (sister of the petitioner no.1), as well as, the respondent no.2 (former wife) are present in the Court and they have been identified by the Investigating Officer, SI Ankur, PS Nihal Vihar.
5. The brief facts of the case are that marriage between the petitioner no.1 and the respondent no.2 was solemnised on 30.11.2019 according to Hindu rites and ceremonies.
6. On account of temperamental issues, certain disputes arose between the parties which led to litigation between them, including registration of the present FIR.
Thereafter, they had been living separately w.e.f. 14.02.2020.

sentences.text:
The parties have now arrived at a settlement, the terms of which have been reduced in writing vide Memorandum of Understanding dated 02.11.2022.
8.

In terms of said agreement, it was agreed between the petitioner no.1 and the respondent no.2 that they will dissolve their marriage by a decree of divorce by mutual consent, which has already been granted by the Family Court on 20.02.2023.
9.

It was also agreed between the parties that the petitioner no.1 shall pay total amount of Rs.4 lakhs to the respondent no.2 towards maintenance (past, present and future) including streedhan,
permanent alimony, etc.

Out of the said amount, Rs. 1 lakh was paid at the time of recording of statement in the first motion petition and another Rs.1 lakh was paid at the time of recording of settlement in the second motion petition, the receipt of which respondent no.2 acknowledges.

The remaining amount of Rs.2 lakhs has been paid today in the Court by the petitioner no.1 to the respondent no.2, by way of demand draft bearing no.027580 dated 15.05.2023 drawn on AXIS Bank Ltd., Bahadurgarh (HR).
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 24/09/2023 at 17:21:56 10.

On a query made by the Court, the respondent no.2 categorically states that she has entered into a compromise with the petitioners out of her own will, without any pressure, coercion or threat and she further states that she has no objection in case the FIR is quashed.

11. In view of the fact that the parties have amicably settled their differences out of their own free will and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served in continuing the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
12. It would, therefore, be in the interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings emanating there from.

13. In view of the above, the present petition is allowed and consequently, the FIR No.1100/2020 under Sections 498A/46/34 IPC registered at PS Nihal Vihar, Delhi and proceedings emanating there from are hereby quashed.
14. The petition is disposed of.
15. Order be uploaded on the website of this Court.
VIKAS MAHAJAN, J MAY 19, 2023 MK
